title: MyISAM storage engine
note: The most important MySQL-only finding. No transactions, no crash recovery, and DMS CDC cannot replicate a MyISAM table -- the binlog records the change but there is no transactional boundary to apply it within. Has no Oracle analogue at all.

title: utf8mb3 columns cannot hold 4-byte characters
note: Legacy `utf8` is 3-byte. Emoji and several CJK ranges truncate. Silent data loss that only appears on the rows containing one, which is why the column charset is the finding rather than the data.

title: No primary key on a high-volume table
note: Worse on MySQL than Oracle: InnoDB creates a hidden 6-byte clustered index DMS cannot address, so CDC has no reliable way to locate a row for UPDATE or DELETE. CDC-only, so on a full-load run it must be marked not-applicable with its reason and keep severity_if_applicable.

title: Zero dates have no PostgreSQL representation
note: '0000-00-00' is not a date PostgreSQL can store. These arrive NULL, which is data loss and cannot be normalised away -- so Phase 8 must report it as a mismatch, not an expected difference. Compare as text: the literal in a WHERE clause is itself rejected under NO_ZERO_DATE.

title: BIGINT UNSIGNED above the PostgreSQL bigint ceiling
note: PostgreSQL bigint is signed, max 9223372036854775807. MySQL unsigned reaches 18446744073709551615. The direct analogue of the Oracle FLOAT -> DOUBLE PRECISION truncation that lost 38 significant digits and was caught ONLY by the level-4 checksum -- row counts and DMS's own error report both missed it. Target type must be numeric.

title: Definer-rights routine
note: RDS grants no SUPER privilege, so a routine whose definer does not exist on the target fails at RUNTIME rather than at migration time.

title: Definer-rights view over PII
note: Same problem as defect 6, harder to spot because a view reads as metadata rather than code. NOTE: SQL SECURITY DEFINER is MySQL's DEFAULT for a view, so the finding is not 'is DEFINER' but 'whose definer will not exist on the target' -- a rule that counts all DEFINER views fires on every clean view too.

title: Reserved-word identifiers
note: Deliberately different words from the Oracle estates. Backtick-quoted on MySQL, double-quoted on PostgreSQL, and any tool or ORM omitting the quotes fails at runtime.

title: Duplicate values in a should-be-unique column
note: Adding the missing unique index on the target fails partway through the load. One duplicate pair differs only in case, which is a duplicate under MySQL's _ci collation and NOT under PostgreSQL's default -- so the count itself changes across engines.

title: Orphaned reference with no foreign key
note: Adding the FK on the target fails; not adding it carries the corruption forward. NOT Oracle's PERF-001 (unindexed foreign key) -- MySQL creates a backing index for every FK automatically, so that defect cannot exist here and a rule reporting it would be reporting something the engine prevents.

title: Redundant index on the same leading column
object: shipment.ix_dup_a is a prefix of ix_dup_ab
note: Earns nothing, costs write time and storage on every insert, and is carried to the target unless someone looks.

title: Sensitive columns in clear text
note: No encryption, no masking, a plain SELECT grant. Moving it unchanged to a cloud target is a decision someone should make knowingly rather than by default.
